$comment: BETA-P0-010 — which service receives which secret. The single source of truth.
Exact allowlists: a service listed with [] receives no secret at all, and a
service that references a secret not listed for it fails the contract. Read by
services/observability/test/compose-secret-distribution.test.ts (hermetic, every
`npm test`) and scripts/check-secret-distribution.mjs (`make secrets-check`, which
resolves the files with `docker compose config`).
Change this file and the compose files in the same commit, and say why in the
commit message: widening a list hands a credential to one more process.
`optionalEmpty` names the only secrets that may use `${NAME:-}`. Every other
reference must be `${NAME:?…}`: a secret is never defaulted, and never defaulted
to another secret.

production.$comment: BETA-P0-012 — the deployment boundary. `exposure: production` switches the published-port rule from loopback-only to exactly publishedPorts.production.

credentialMounts.$comment: Credentials delivered as files rather than variables, and the only service allowed to mount each.

$comment: BETA-P0-011 — host ports that carry a credential. Read by the same two enforcers.
`never`: the sandboxd capability port. Its callers reach it on a private network;
publishing it would put the attach, runtime and Docker endpoints on the host.
`loopbackOnly`: the api and terminal ports (INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET) and the three
metrics listeners (OBSERVABILITY_SCRAPE_TOKEN). Published, if at all, on 127.0.0.1.
BETA-P0-012 — every stack, not just the credential ports:
`loopbackOnly` now lists every container port a development stack may publish, and
each must bind 127.0.0.1. A port not listed fails, so a new publication is reviewed.
PostgreSQL (5432), the web tier (3000) and Prometheus/Alertmanager (9090, 9093) joined.
`production`: a stack with `exposure: production` publishes exactly these entries and
nothing else, on any interface — loopback included. 443 must reach nginx's TLS listener
and 80 its redirect-only listener; `443:3000` (plaintext on the HTTPS port) fails.
Only `ports:` counts. `expose:` and Dockerfile EXPOSE are metadata and publish nothing.
BETA-P0-012 — networks whose members are an exact allowlist, read by the same two
enforcers. `database` holds PostgreSQL and the one service with its credential, so a
student shell in the terminal container has no route to it. `internalIn` names the
stacks where the network must also be `internal: true` (no route off the host).
